characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Field emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FEI Quanta-650 FEG)
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN850 shows blocky/equiaxed ferrite grains outlined by bainite, with thin film-like retained austenite and blocky fresh martensite (Fig. 2(e)).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etching with 4% nitric acid ethanol solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the multiphase microstructure of AN850

characterization_methods.key_findings: AN850 phase fractions FCC 0.002 / BCC 0.998; RA average grain size D_AVE = 0.83 µm; RA content 0.2 vol%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 20 kV operating voltage; 0.2 µm scanning step; BCC and FCC phases indexed; minimum pixel size 9
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase distribution and retained austenite size quantification for AN850

characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD confirms the decrease in retained austenite content with increasing annealing temperature (Fig. 3(f)).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Rolling plane of the sample; accelerating voltage 40 kV; tube current 40 mA; scanning angle range 30°–110°
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and confirmation of the retained austenite trend

interfaces.interface_notes: Bainite distributes along ferrite grain boundaries, and fresh martensite or FM+RA islands are attached to the bainite.
interfaces.phase_evolution: During intercritical annealing, portions of bainite and martensite reaustenitize due to the high solubility of carbon in austenite; carbon-depleted regions form ferrite, some carbon-enriched austenite is retained during cooling as RA, unstabilized austenite transforms to fresh martensite, and bainite forms during cooling in regions not fully austenitized.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 39 kg low-density steel ingot with the composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P was produced via vacuum induction melting.
The ingot was hot forged and cut into billets measuring 90 mm (length) x 70 mm (width) x 40 mm (thickness).
These billets were heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min.

Hot rolling on a high-rigidity two-roll mill beginning at 1100 °C; six passes with a cumulative reduction rate of 90%, yielding plates with a final thickness of 4 mm; finish rolling completed at 880 °C followed by air cooling.
Cold rolling was performed on a four-roll reversible mill with a 60% reduction rate, resulting in plates with a thickness of 1.6 mm.
The cold-rolled sample was annealed at 850 °C for 30 min within the critical region and air-cooled to room temperature, labeled AN850.

phases_present.morphology: Blocky/equiaxed ferrite grains outlined by bainite
Bainite distributed along ferrite grain boundaries
Blocky fresh martensite attached to bainite or islands comprising fresh martensite and retained austenite
Thin film-like retained austenite between ferrite grains

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase heterogeneous microstructure composed of ferrite (F), bainite (B), fresh martensite (FM) and retained austenite (RA); blocky/equiaxed ferrite grains are outlined by bainite, with thin film-like retained austenite and blocky fresh martensite. EBSD phase fractions: FCC 0.002 / BCC 0.998; retained austenite content 0.2 vol%.

unmapped_findings: The paper reports tensile mechanical properties (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation) only for the low-bainite-aged variants AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T; no tensile properties are reported for the intercritically annealed AN850 sample itself.

AN850 is the highest annealing-temperature state among the three intercritically annealed samples; its retained austenite content (0.2 vol%) is the lowest and its RA average grain size (0.83 µm) is the largest among AN750, AN800 and AN850.
